title: Developer onboarding workshop: runtime SLOs, local loop & telemetry contracts
author: Maya Patel
content:
Overview:
This page is a hands-on workshop and playbook aimed at developer-facing teams who are onboarding to the Redwood runtime and SDK stack. It covers the local development loop, telemetry contracts between SDKs and the platform, concrete runtime SLOs to design against, and canonical fixes for common developer-facing support issues. The goal is to provide a one-hour workshop template plus a reproducible checklist and code snippets that engineering teams can adopt with minimal changes.

Audience:
- SDK engineers and developer-product teams
- Integration engineers embedding Redwood APIs into product flows
- Solutions engineers and support engineers running onboarding sessions

Goals:
1) Reduce first-time integration time by 40% (measured by time to a green sanity test)
2) Ensure every integration emits the minimum telemetry contract so platform dashboards can aggregate meaningful metrics
3) Teach a standard troubleshooting flow that maps symptom → root cause → canonical fix

Prerequisites:
- Access to a Redwood sandbox account and API key (dev-stage)
- Local developer environment with Docker and Node 18+ or Python 3.10+
- repo: git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/devx-workshop-starter.git
- Optional: access to the local telemetry collector (devx-otel) in your org VPC

Workshop agenda (60 minutes):
1) 5m — Intro & desired outcomes
2) 10m — Quick local loop demo (dx-local-proxy + sample app)
3) 15m — Telemetry contract overview and example events
4) 15m — Hands-on integration: wire SDK, assert SLOs, run sanity test
5) 10m — Canonical fixes & Q/A

Quick local loop (step-by-step):
1) Start the local proxy and telemetry stub:
   - dx-local-proxy is a lightweight shim that translates local SDK calls to the sandbox API and collects spans.
   - Command: ``dx-local-proxy start --env sandbox --port 6060``
2) Configure your SDK to point at the local proxy (example for JavaScript):
   - env: REDWOOD_API_BASE=http://localhost:6060
   - code snippet:

```javascript
const Redwood = require('@redwood/sdk');
const client = new Redwood({ baseUrl: process.env.REDWOOD_API_BASE, apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
const resp = await client.generate({ model: 'rw-small', prompt: 'Hello, world' });
console.log(resp.text);
```

3) Run the built-in sanity test suite: ``npm run smoke:test`` (should pass within 15s locally).

Telemetry contract (minimum required events):
- request.start (tags: sdk_name, sdk_version, route, model, request_id)
- request.end (tags: status_code, token_count, latency_ms, request_id)
- cache.hit / cache.miss (tags: key, route)
- kv-cache.size (gauge)
- client.error (tags: error_type, http_status, request_id)

Recommended event schema (JSON example):
```json
{
  "event": "request.end",
  "tags": {"sdk_name": "js-sdk","sdk_version": "0.7.1","route": "generation","model": "rw-small","status_code": 200,"token_count": 42,"latency_ms": 123} 
}
```

Runtime SLOs and thresholds (developer-facing):
- Developer local loop (sanity test): median < 150ms, p95 < 600ms for a single short prompt (this is local/network bound)
- Hosted API (developer tier): p50 < 120ms, p95 < 350ms for text-generation small models; error rate < 0.5% per minute
- Dedicated testing tier: sustained throughput target 500 req/s for rw-medium with 8 GPU pool; tail latency p99 < 700ms
- Telemetry ingestion SLO: 99% of events should be ingested and visible in dashboards within 60s

Configuration table (copy/paste friendly):
- key: local_proxy.port, value: 6060
- key: sdk.default_timeout_ms, value: 20000
- key: telemetry.batch_interval_ms, value: 5000
- key: telemetry.endpoint, value: https://devx-otel.redwood.internal/ingest

Sanity test checklist (one-click smoke):
1) Set env: REDWOOD_API_KEY, REDWOOD_API_BASE
2) Start dx-local-proxy
3) Run ``npm run smoke:test`` or ``pytest tests/smoke.py``
4) Verify telemetry shows request.start and request.end with the same request_id
5) Confirm p95 latency is below the local threshold and no client.error events emitted

Canonical support issues and fixes (symptom → cause → canonical fix):
1) Symptom: SDK returns 502 intermittently during long generation flows
   - Cause: local proxy hitting default proxy timeout; upstream chunking mismatch
   - Fix: increase dx-local-proxy timeout with ENV DX_PROXY_TIMEOUT_MS=45000 and switch SDK streaming mode to chunked-stream. If repro in hosted: escalate to infra with trace and request_id.

2) Symptom: Missing telemetry events in platform dashboard for some requests
   - Cause: telemetry batching config too aggressive or transient network failures between dx-local-proxy and devx-otel
   - Fix: set telemetry.batch_interval_ms to 2000 during integration, enable retry backoff in dx-local-proxy (config: telemetry.retry.max_retries = 5). Use trace id present in request.start to search raw logs.

3) Symptom: Higher than expected token_count reported in billing dashboard vs client expectation
   - Cause: prompt composition performed on server (server-side templates) or double-encoding of prompt+system messages
   - Fix: add local instrumentation to assert request payload length before send. Use sample payload inspection: ``REDWOOD_DEBUG_PAYLOAD=1``. Update SDK integration to use structured messages API instead of concatenating system+prompt.

4) Symptom: p95 latency spike correlated with cache misses
   - Cause: global cache TTL misconfiguration or key namespace collision
   - Fix: rotate cache namespace for the integration (config cache.namespace = "team-a-<date>"), preload common prefixes, and enable kv-cache warmup in deployment script. Verify kv-cache.size gauge increases after preload.

Troubleshooting flow (short):
1) Reproduce locally with dx-local-proxy and smoke test.
2) Collect the request_id from the failing run.
3) Confirm presence/absence of request.start and request.end in devx-otel.
4) If events exist, inspect latency_ms and token_count tags; if not, escalate to telemetry team with trace export.

Post-workshop deliverables (for workshop owner to share):
- A fork of devx-workshop-starter with the team-specific README and env examples
- A short recording of the 20m demo section (hosted on internal drive)
- A checklist card in the team’s onboarding board with acceptance criteria (smoke tests green, telemetry events visible, SLOs met)

Owner & escalation path:
- Primary owner: Developer Experience (team lead: Maya Patel)
- Escalation: oncall-devx@redwood.com → eng-sre if platform-level traces show systemic issues

Metrics to track post-onboard (KPIs):
- Mean time to first green (MTFG) for new integrations (goal < 2 hours)
- % of integrations emitting full telemetry contract (goal 95%)
- Number of support tickets opened within first 30 days post-integration (goal < 2 per integration)

Appendix — Useful commands and snippets:
- Start proxy (docker): ``docker run --rm -p 6060:6060 redwood/dx-local-proxy:latest start --env sandbox``
- Export debug payloads: ``export REDWOOD_DEBUG_PAYLOAD=1; npm run smoke:test``
- Example Python client config:

```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(base_url='http://localhost:6060', api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY'])
resp = client.generate(model='rw-small', prompt='Explain event-driven design')
print(resp.text)
```
